new_candidates.body:
## Desired behavior

*The PRs of this series are open as drafts and linked below. Bold labels (**08b**, **09b**, …) are prepared branches that wait on the questions here. The OgreNext PR (**15**) will follow.*

Depth cameras, RGBD cameras and GPU lidars should cost less CPU per simulated second, and let gz-sim run faster at RTF 0, while publishing the same messages as today. Some PRs in this series add public API in gz-rendering, gz-sensors and gz-transport, so I would like to agree on that API before opening them. A few further gains change the output; for those I'd like to know whether you want them at all, as opt-in options.

gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 (readback wait) is already open; the rendering PRs below build on it.

**Setup.** ANYmal on MuJoCo at a 1.25 ms step, RTX 4070, headless EGL. Main scenario: six 640x480 depth cameras at 15 Hz. CPU: gz-sim server CPU seconds per simulated second, pinned to 1 core. Wall: simulated seconds per wall second on 3 cores. Both at RTF 0, n=5 runs of 20 s per arm, arms interleaved, mean ± 95% CI. Base: gz-sensors 8ddf4c1, gz-rendering fb8e38ce, gz-transport 41913b9d, gz-sim 71c60db31.

On main with six depth cameras, physics waits for the render thread 61% of the wall time. Each camera waits for its own GPU-to-CPU transfer in `PostRender()`, one camera after another. A frame with no point cloud subscriber still reads back the full RGBA32F point cloud texture (4.9 MB at 640x480). The sensor then copies the frame two or three more times before the message reaches the transport.

## Changes with byte-identical output (PRs ready)

Each row is one PR measured alone on top of the PRs it needs (the base column). The messages are unchanged; see the next section for how this was checked.

**Render ahead** (overlap the readbacks of several sensors)

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392 (16a) + #697 (16b) | `Camera::IssueReadback()`; `Manager::RunOnce` renders every due depth camera and GPU lidar and issues their readbacks, then runs each `Update()` | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 | depth images −6.9%; with `/points` −9.1%; three 2048x128 lidars −1.3% (noise) | **+39%**; **+40%**; **+13%** |
| #698 (19) | the same for `RgbdCameraSensor` (six 640x480 RGBD cameras) | 16b | image −7.9%; all topics −7.8% | image **+24.5%**; depth **+53.1%**; all topics **+47.2%** |

**Depth camera**

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1393 (07) | with no point cloud subscriber, render and read back only the R32 depth (1.2 MB instead of 4.9 MB), in one quad pass, without unread clears | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 | depth images **−31.6%**; with `/points` no change | **+58%**; no change |
| #699 (08) | `DepthCameraSensor`: copy the frame once, fill the cloud in one pass, publish image and cloud in place (needs 05) | main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + 05 | depth images **−12.4%**; `/points` ZeroMQ **−33.2%**, Zenoh **−38.1%** | **+25%**; **+50%**, **+68%** |
| gazebosim/gz-rendering#1394 (09a) + **08b** | the rendering camera can deliver packed xyz (12 instead of 16 bytes per point, no colour pass); the sensor asks for it, since its `rgb` field is a grayscale of the depth anyway | 07 / 08 | 09a alone: no change (nothing asks for packed yet) | |

Stack 16 + 07 + 09a + 08 + 08b against main + gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 + 16 + 05, depth images and `/points` over Zenoh SHM (64 MiB pool): CPU 0.4134 ± 0.0078 → 0.1825 ± 0.0042 (−56%), wall 2.53 ± 0.08 → 5.76 ± 0.30 (2.3×).

**Publish in place** (gz-transport API and its users)

| PR | change | base | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (05) | `Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`: the caller writes the serialized message straight into the buffer the transport sends | main | no change alone (no caller) | no change |
| #693 (06) | lidar scan and points in place (one 2048x128 lidar) | main + 01 + 02 + 05 | ZeroMQ −6.6%, Zenoh **−6.9%** | not resolved |
| #694 (14) | camera image in place (six 640x480 cameras) | main + 05 | −2.9% (noise) | **+7.0% ± 6.2** |
| #695 (17) | RGBD depth image in place (depth subscribed) | main + 05 | **−10.6%** | **+21.4%** |
| #696 (18) | RGBD point cloud and image in place | 17 | image only **−32.9%**; all topics **−21.7%** | **+20.1%**; +37.8% ± 27.9 |

(08 above is also a user of 05.)

## How equivalence was checked

- gz-sim main with the PRs against unmodified gz-sim main. A sink in another process records every message of every sensor topic; each message's raw bytes are compared by CRC, matched by header stamp.
- Worlds: four depth worlds (static, moving, 16 moving boxes, 16 boxes spawned and removed between renders), three cameras each, depth images and `/points`; three lidar worlds (static, moving, Gaussian noise with a fixed seed); five RGBD worlds (static, moving, transition, noise, toggle). ZeroMQ or Zenoh, as stated in each PR.
- A toggle test: point cloud subscribers connect and leave during the run while a model moves into the forward camera's view. It checks the first cloud after a subscriber connects and the first cloud of the run.
- Each PR has unit or integration tests that fail when its change is perturbed.

**Toggle test start-up.** Earlier toggle runs differed on the forward camera from t=1.667 s on, where the moving model enters its view, also on unmodified gz-sim main (2 of 7 runs). The cause was our harness: the `gz sim` CLI creates the world's models and systems on a background thread unless `--wait-for-assets` is given, so the world stepped empty for a variable number of iterations. With `--wait-for-assets` the toggle test is identical to gz main in 25 of 25 runs on the depth PRs (16a + 16b, 07, 09a, 08, and the stack 16 + 07 + 09a + 08 + 08b; 5 each) and in 5 of 5 on the RGBD one (19).

## Questions for maintainers

0. **Is this split OK?** One change per PR, stacked as listed: 16a/16b after gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391; 07 then 09a; 05 before its users (06, 08, 14, 17, 18); 08b after 08 and 09a.

1. **`Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace`** (gazebosim/gz-transport#993 (05), details in gazebosim/gz-transport#992).
   Proposal: `bool PublishInPlace(std::size_t _msgSize, const std::function<bool(char *_buffer)> &_serialize)`. The buffer is a Zenoh SHM chunk when the message goes through shared memory, otherwise a heap buffer handed to ZeroMQ or Zenoh. Local subscribers, ordering, throttling and `IgnoreLocalMessages` behave as with `Publish()`. Is a new member on `Publisher` in this shape acceptable?

2. **`Camera::IssueReadback()` and `Sensor::RenderAhead()`** (gazebosim/gz-rendering#1392 (16a), #697 (16b)).
   Proposal: `virtual bool Camera::IssueReadback()`, default false, one name for every camera type (RGB can implement it later). On `Sensor`, a protected virtual `RenderAhead()` (default false, serial), a public `RenderAheadIfDue()` for the Manager, and a protected `RenderedAhead()`. Both add virtuals, so this is an ABI break: main only, and gz-sim must be rebuilt. One order change: a listener attached directly to a rendering camera's frame events runs after the whole run has rendered, not between cameras. The sensors' own callbacks are not affected. Is that OK for main?

3. **Packed xyz point cloud format** (gazebosim/gz-rendering#1394 (09a), **08b**).
   Proposal: `DepthCamera::SetPointCloudFormat(PixelFormat)` with `PF_FLOAT32_RGBA` (default) or `PF_FLOAT32_RGB`. Should it be a pixel format or a boolean "xyz only"? Should `DepthCameraSensor` ask for it for every cloud (08b)? The published messages don't change, but a listener connected directly to `DepthCamera()->ConnectNewRgbPointCloud()` then gets three floats per point instead of four. Or should the sensor ask for it only when configured to?

**Opt-in behaviours.** These change the output, so they would be off by default. I'm asking about each one separately.

4. **16-bit millimetre depth** (09b, branch prepared, no tests yet).
   `<image><format>L_INT16</format>` gives `uint16` depth in mm, as real 16UC1 cameras do (REP 118): 0 means invalid, values are rounded to the nearest mm, and the GPU does the conversion (`DepthCamera::SetDepthImageFormat(PF_L16)`). On the prototype stack, depth image only: 0.083 → 0.065 CPU s per sim s (not measured alone on the current branch). Should the 16-bit frame go through the existing `newDepthFrame` event (a format string, with the `const float *` pointing at `uint16_t` data, as in the prototype), or through a typed `ConnectNewDepthFrame16` like the thermal camera's?

5. **xyz-only point clouds** (09d, branch prepared, no tests yet).
   This drops the grayscale `rgb` field (`point_step` 16 → 12). Most consumers (SLAM, costmaps) ignore it. Prototype stack, `/points` over Zenoh: 0.150 / 6.37 → 0.107 / 9.95 (CPU s per sim s / sim s per wall s). Do you want this option?

6. **Deferred readback** (09c; no PR, asked only as an opt-in question).
   `PostRender()` maps the readback of frame N−1, which the GPU has finished, instead of waiting for frame N. The stamp stays the render time, but the data arrives one sensor period late in sim time, and the first update publishes nothing. That rules it out for closed-loop perception; it could suit datasets, stamp-aligned SLAM and RL. Its case is `/points` wall speed: 6.37 → 9.24 sim s per wall s (+45%) on the prototype stack. With gazebosim/gz-rendering#1391 it gives nothing for depth images alone. Render ahead (16) closes most of the gap without any delay: in another batch on the same prototype stack, 5.64 → 7.44 against 7.58 with deferred readback (93% of the gap). Is there interest in this as an opt-in, or should it stay out?

7. **Where should the switches live** (for 4 to 6, and 3 if it becomes opt-in)? An SDF element (for example under `<depth_camera>`, which needs a matching sdformat PR), or a `Sensors` system parameter / sensor API? 16-bit depth can use the existing `<image><format>`.

## Pre-existing bugs found along the way

I can file these separately:

- gz-sensors: `DepthCameraSensor::SetScene()` keeps the point cloud connection on the old camera, and so does `RgbdCameraSensor`. After a scene change, main keeps republishing the last cloud (and, for RGBD, the last image) with new stamps.
- gz-sensors: a sensor that removes itself from its own callback is a use-after-free in `Sensor::Update()`, because the callback runs inside the sensor's method.
- gz-rendering (ogre2): destroying a depth camera while its scene stays alive, then creating another one, trips Ogre's `HlmsDatablock` assertion ("still being used by some Renderables"), the same assertion as gazebosim/gz-sensors#548 (closed; the fix was planned in gz-rendering). Removing an `RgbdCameraSensor` from its `Manager` while the scene lives does the same. It happens on main, with the packaged OgreNext as well.
- Already fixed in this series: an out-of-bounds write in `Lidar` for `<resolution>` > 1 (#691 (01)), and a data race in `Lidar::ApplyNoise`, which wrote the buffer without `lidarMutex` (#693 (06)).

## Additional context

- Zenoh can fall back from shared memory without any message: gazebosim/gz-transport#991.
- ros_gz_bridge maps `L_INT16` to `mono16`. depth_image_proc accepts that, and a small ros_gz change could add `16UC1`.
- Related PRs that change no API: gz-sensors lidar #691 (01), #692 (02); gz-rendering RGB readback gazebosim/gz-rendering#1395 (12), gazebosim/gz-rendering#1396 (13); OgreNext ForwardClustered **15**.

new_candidates.body:
## Desired behavior

When `GZ_TRANSPORT_IMPLEMENTATION=zenoh` is set and a message that should travel through shared memory does not, print a message on stderr once, with the reason and the setting to change. Today the fallback is silent, and the fallback path can be slower than ZeroMQ.

## Current behavior

Measured on gz-transport main (41913b9d) with zenoh-c / zenoh-cpp 1.8.0, using six 640x480 depth cameras and a 2048x128 GPU lidar (ANYmal on MuJoCo, our quadruped bench):

- The default 48 MiB pool is more than the stock 8 MiB locked-memory limit (`ulimit -l`) allows, both on the host and in docker. The session's SHM provider goes from `SHM_PROVIDER_INITIALIZING` to `SHM_PROVIDER_ERROR`, and messages to other processes on the host go through the network stack, which is slower than ZeroMQ. Nothing is printed.
- A pool larger than the free space in `/dev/shm` gives the same `SHM_PROVIDER_ERROR`. Docker's default `/dev/shm` is 64 MB, so a 64 MiB pool also needs `--shm-size`. On our lidar branch this fallback cost 0.097 instead of 0.067 CPU s per sim s, and three bench batches ran like this before we found the cause.
- Both cases behave the same in `lazy` and `init` mode, and opening the session never fails. `SHM_PROVIDER_DISABLED` only comes from the configuration switch. (Checked with a small program that polls `obtain_shm_provider()`, zenoh 1.8.0.)
- A 6 MiB pool (`GZ_TRANSPORT_ZENOH_CONFIG_OVERRIDE="transport/shared_memory/transport_optimization/pool_size=6291456"`) fits the 8 MiB limit, and shared memory is then used.
- With `/points` subscribed, six 4.9 MB clouds don't fit in 6 MiB. Allocation fails, and those messages go through the network stack, again slower than ZeroMQ, again without a message. Point clouds need a pool of at least 32 MiB **and** a raised memlock limit.

## Implementation suggestion

1. When `obtain_shm_provider()` returns `SHM_PROVIDER_ERROR`, print one warning with the configuration key and, on Linux, the current `ulimit -l` and the free space in `/dev/shm`. Print nothing for `SHM_PROVIDER_DISABLED`, since the user asked for it.
2. The first time `allocShmChunk()` fails for a message at or above the threshold (pool full, or smaller than the message), print one warning with the message size and the configuration key.
3. Document the memlock and `/dev/shm` requirements in the environment-variable tutorial.

The fallback, the defaults and the published bytes stay as they are. This is implemented and tested on a branch; I'll open the PR after this issue.

## Question

Should the default pool follow the memlock limit (a smaller default when 48 MiB can't be locked), or stay at 48 MiB with the warning? The PR leaves the default alone.

new_candidates.body:
## Desired behavior

A publisher of large messages (images, point clouds, lidar scans) should be able to write the serialized message straight into the buffer that the transport sends, so the payload is written once.

Today the sensor copies the payload into a protobuf message, and `Publish()` then serializes that message into the outgoing buffer: a 640x480 depth image is 1.2 MB, and its point cloud is 4.9 MB. This is part of gazebosim/gz-sensors#690.

## Implementation suggestion

A new member of `Node::Publisher`:

```cpp
bool Node::Publisher::PublishInPlace(
    std::size_t _msgSize,
    const std::function<bool(char *_buffer)> &_serialize);
```

- `_serialize` writes exactly `_msgSize` bytes, a serialized message of the advertised type, and returns false to cancel. It isn't called when nobody subscribes or the publication is throttled.
- The buffer is a Zenoh shared-memory chunk when Zenoh delivers through shared memory. Otherwise it is a heap buffer whose ownership passes to ZeroMQ or Zenoh. Remote subscribers keep the zero-copy path.
- Local (in-process) and raw subscribers are called on the publish thread, ordered with `Publish()` calls, as `Publish()` does. Raw handlers get a copy of the buffer, or the buffer itself when there is no remote subscriber. Typed handlers get the message parsed from it. The copy or parse happens only when such subscribers exist.
- `IgnoreLocalMessages` and throttling work as in `Publish()`. A publisher advertised with the generic message type is rejected.
- No new data members. For a message `m`, `PublishInPlace(m.ByteSizeLong(), <write m>)` sends the same bytes as `Publish(m)`.

It is implemented and tested in #993 (part of the series in gazebosim/gz-sensors#690): the whole suite passes with ZeroMQ and with Zenoh, and there are two new tests for callback threading and ordering against `Publish()`.

Measured on its own, it changes nothing, because nothing calls it yet. These sensor PRs use it, each measured alone on top of 05. The setup is ANYmal on MuJoCo, RTX 4070, RTF 0; CPU is server CPU s per sim s on 1 core, wall is sim s per wall s on 3 cores, n=5:

| user | CPU, 1 core | wall, 3 cores |
|---|---|---|
| gazebosim/gz-sensors#693 (06): one 2048x128 lidar, scan and points | ZeroMQ −6.6%, Zenoh −6.9% | not resolved |
| gazebosim/gz-sensors#699 (08): six 640x480 depth cameras (also copies the frame once) | depth images −12.4%; with `/points` ZeroMQ −33.2%, Zenoh −38.1% | +25%; +50%, +68% |
| gazebosim/gz-sensors#694 (14): six 640x480 cameras | −2.9% (noise) | +7.0% ± 6.2 |
| gazebosim/gz-sensors#695 (17): six RGBD cameras, depth image | −10.6% | +21.4% |
| gazebosim/gz-sensors#696 (18): six RGBD cameras, image / all topics | −32.9% / −21.7% | +20.1% / +37.8% ± 27.9 |

In each case the published bytes match `Publish()` of the message built the old way. This is checked by the sensor tests and end to end, by a CRC of every raw message in another process compared against gz main.

## Questions

- Is a new member on `Publisher` in this shape acceptable, given that it is a callback that writes into a buffer the transport provides?
- Services and the generic message type aren't covered. Is that fine for a first version?

## Additional context

- Zero-copy from the GPU readback into shared memory isn't possible with Ogre's GL backend, so one copy (readback buffer → outgoing buffer) remains.
- The users write the protobuf wire format themselves. The depth camera PR (08), for example, serializes the header fields in order, then the data tag and length, then copies the frame straight from the render engine's buffer. Their tests compare the bytes with `Publish()`.

new_candidates.body:
### Description

`release_instance()` in `OgnROS2CameraHelper.py` (L365) and `OgnROS2RtxLidarHelper.py` (L366) calls:

```python
state = OgnROS2CameraHelperInternalState.per_instance_internal_state(node)
```

`per_instance_internal_state` is defined on the generated `OgnROS2CameraHelperDatabase` / `OgnROS2RtxLidarHelperDatabase` classes, not on the `...InternalState` (`BaseWriterNode`) classes. The resulting `AttributeError` is swallowed by `except Exception: state = None`, so `cleanup_srtx_state()` and `state.reset()` never run, and the Replicator writer stays attached to `/Render/PostProcess/SDGPipeline` after the helper node or its graph is deleted.

### Effect

When a graph containing the helper (and its `ROS2Context` node) is deleted while the timeline is playing:

- Writers that have not created their ROS node yet try every frame with the deleted context handle and log:
  ```
  [Error] [omni.graph.core.plugin] /Render/PostProcess/SDGPipeline/Replicator_NodeWriterWriter: [/Render/PostProcess/SDGPipeline] Unable to create ROS2 node, please check that namespace is valid
  ```
  This message is misleading; the namespace is fine, and the context handle is gone.
- Writers that already have a node keep publishing. If the graph is recreated, the topic is published twice. In our test, every `LaserScan` on `/scan_front` arrived twice with the same stamp.

Stopping the timeline before deleting the graph avoids it.

### Reproduction

1. Create an OmniGraph with `ROS2Context` + `IsaacCreateRenderProduct` + `ROS2RtxLidarHelper` (or `ROS2CameraHelper`) and press Play.
2. While playing, delete the graph prim and create the same graph again.
3. Depending on timing, observe the error above every frame, or duplicate messages on the topic.

### Suggested fix

```python
state = OgnROS2CameraHelperDatabase.per_instance_internal_state(node)  # likewise for the LiDAR helper
```

### Workaround we use

Before deleting the graph, we call `OgnROS2...HelperDatabase.per_instance_internal_state(node).custom_reset()`, which queues `writer.detach()` for the next update. With this, the error count drops to 0 and the duplicates disappear.

### Environment

Isaac Sim 6.0.1-rc.7 (`isaacsim.ros2.nodes` 1.18.13), reproduced on Ubuntu 24.04 / ROS 2 Jazzy and Ubuntu 22.04 / ROS 2 Humble (internal ROS libraries).


### Isaac Sim version

6.0.1

### Operating System (OS)

Ubuntu 24.04

### GPU Name

RTX 6000 Ada

### GPU Driver and CUDA versions

Driver 595.99.02 / CUDA 13.2

### Logs

[Error] [omni.graph.core.plugin] /Render/PostProcess/SDGPipeline/Replicator_NodeWriterWriter: [/Render/PostProcess/SDGPipeline] Unable to create ROS2 node, please check that namespace is valid

### Additional information

_No response_
